distinguish_from.distinction: A nonnull pointer only excludes the null value. Receiver/table association additionally requires that every selected operation interprets the live receiver as its actual concrete representation; an unrelated nonnull table can still violate that contract.

Deep copying would recursively create independent owned referents under an explicit policy; copying an environment containing a pointer preserves the alias, not an independent referent.

idiom: State the capture environment invariant before publishing the object or callback.

distinguish_from.distinction: A thunk is an actual adapter with the erased interface compatible function type; it decodes or recovers the concrete state and makes a correctly typed call. Casting an unrelated function pointer does not adapt its calling contract or make an incompatible call valid.

idiom: State the invocation thunk invariant before publishing the object or callback.

A borrowed callable provides invocation without taking that ownership; even an owning wrapper can retain borrowed references inside its capture whose lifetimes must be established separately.

idiom: State the erased callable owner invariant before publishing the object or callback.

distinguish_from.distinction: Embedded links establish container membership and constrain movement while linked. Payload ownership determines who may destroy or reclaim the object; unlinking may end membership without releasing payload ownership, and a container must not infer ownership merely from a link.

distinguish_from.distinction: Attenuation removes rights from an existing authority under the enforcing protocol. Amplification adds authority that the source did not possess; the subset check must reject it, and caller-editable C fields alone are not an unforgeable enforcement boundary.

idiom: State the authority attenuation invariant before publishing the object or callback.

distinguish_from.distinction: A loaded-code borrow is a protocol obligation to keep the owning module valid until all derived API and callback uses end. A mapped address describes current virtual-memory state; continued mapping after logical close does not renew the borrow or authorize stale calls.

idiom: State the loaded-code borrow invariant before publishing the object or callback.
entries.misconception: A retained mapping after close does not renew the protocol lifetime.

entries.definition: A declared state in which no admitted user can still invoke or access code/data scheduled for retirement.

distinguish_from.distinction: Quiescence excludes every admitted future use of retiring code and data, including held API borrows and queued callbacks. Having no active stack frame excludes only calls executing at that instant and can leave future accesses possible.

idiom: State the reload quiescence invariant before publishing the object or callback.
entries.misconception: Queued callbacks and retained data may still prevent retirement.

entries.definition: Explicit retained ownership of an old module after a new one is committed and before cleanup completes.

idiom: State the retired module owner invariant before publishing the object or callback.
entries.misconception: Cleanup failure after commit does not mean the old state was never replaced.
